messages:
kim: heads up — acme wants a POC commit but with a weird billing ask: they want autoscale up to 12 A100-equivalent GPUs during spikes, but only pay for a soft cap and have overage smoothed into a monthly credit. can we structure that?
raj: do they mean hard guarantee of capacity or just burstable headroom?
ellie: they said reserved baseline 4 gpus, burst to 12 for short windows. emphasis on predictable cost during POC.
jordan-sales: they also want a 30-day trial with no penalties for exceeding the soft cap during POC, plus weekly usage reports. they flagged SLA for latency too.
sam-ops: technically we can map this to a reserved pool (4 gpus baseline) + burst buckets. question: what billing model? per-minute metering vs per-hour buckets changes the math.
maria-legal: we'll need to add a POC addendum for billing smoothing and an explicit definition of "soft cap" vs "hard cap". also need acceptance criteria for rollout.
kims: @sam-ops can you sketch SLO/routing behavior? i.e., if baseline saturated do we queue or route to hosted fallback? acme expects graceful degradation not errors.
sam-ops: plan: baseline serves up to 4, continuous batching enabled. burst policy: allow up to 12 for short windows up to 15 minutes / 6x per day. after bursts are exhausted requests route to hosted-compatible model variant in eu-west fallback.
raj: ok can we propose the following commercial terms?
```
- Baseline: 4 A100-equivalent GPUs reserved (monthly commit)
- Burst: up to +8 GPUs available during spikes, limited to 15 minutes per burst, 6 bursts/day
- Billing: baseline billed at commit rate; burst usage billed at discounted overage rate up to a monthly soft cap; over-soft-cap usage converted to monthly credit smoothing at 75% of list overage price
- Metering window: 1-minute granularity for billing calculations
```
jordan-sales: acme will want the discounted overage rate down from list — can we offer 20% off for the POC period?
sam-ops: operationally 20% off is tight but doable for short POC if we cap bursts frequency. need engineering signoff for the 1-minute metering accuracy and telemetry export.
maria-legal: add clause: "if burst abuse pattern > X, Redwood may throttle to baseline or negotiate additional commit" — recommended.
billing-bot: FYI: estimated cost with the proposed structure (30-day POC, expected 10 bursts at avg 10 GPUs for 10 minutes) => approx $18,400 before discounts. (internal calc)
ellie: acme also submitted a security questionnaire asking about data residency during bursts (they want EU-only GPUs). can we guarantee region pinning for burst instances?
sam-ops: yes—routing policy can constrain bursts to eu-west capacity only. need to confirm capacity in that region for requested windows.
kim: next steps: 1) @sam-ops validate eu-west available capacity for the requested burst windows and confirm metering accuracy, 2) @raj and @jordan-sales draft deal desk note with the proposed 20% POC overage discount and soft-cap smoothing language, 3) @maria-legal draft POC addendum with throttling/abuse clause and acceptance criteria, 4) export sample usage report template for acme.
raj: i'll open a deal-desk ticket and cc pricing@. want to include a short cost sensitivity table — can someone grab the numbers from billing?
billing-bot: attached: sample CSV (s3 link) and quick sensitivity: 10% change in burst minutes -> ~ $1.8k swing.
jordan-sales: tagging acme contact (cc) to confirm they accept eu-west-only constraint: @acme-poc.
kims: nice. please keep updates here. :thumbsup:
